# dsh-mobile-pwa

> Complete mobile PWA for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): secure remote access gateway + install-to-homescreen + offline + touch gestures + agent-done push.

## Key facts
- Repo: zylzyqzz/dsh-mobile-pwa. MIT license, `dsh-plugin` topic. Derivative of `dsh-mobile-gate` (MIT).
- Targets **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x** (`engines.dsh: ">=0.2.0 <0.3.0"`). The 0.1.x Web-UI DOM is gone; the CSS now targets the 0.2 slot vocabulary.
- Install: `npm add dsh-mobile-pwa` then `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mobile-pwa` (or `dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-mobile-pwa` for a checkout).
- Architecture: standalone child-process Node gateway (zero-dep), reverse-proxies approved LAN/remote devices to the DSH Web UI; DSH's own webserver is never rebound. DSH 0.2 refuses a wildcard bind address, so this gateway is the remote door.
- Target address is resolved from the `webStartup` service (`dsh web --host/--port`), not hardcoded; the plugin passes it to the child explicitly because DSH 0.2 scrubs the child environment.
- Gateway serves `/pwa/*` assets (manifest, sw.js, app.css, icons, offline.html) + `/pwa/push/*` (real Web Push: RFC 8291 aes128gcm body, RFC 8292 VAPID auth).
- Agent-done detection lives in the browser: DSH 0.2 renders `[data-chat-running]` while the agent works; when it disappears the page raises a notification and reports it to the gateway.
- Env: `LAN_GATE_PORT` (3088), `LAN_GATE_HOST` (0.0.0.0), `LAN_GATE_TARGET_HOST` (127.0.0.1), `LAN_GATE_TARGET_PORT` (3080), `LAN_GATE_RATE_LIMIT` (120), `LAN_GATE_VAPID_PUBLICKEY`, `LAN_GATE_VAPID_PRIVATEKEY`, `LAN_GATE_VAPID_SUBJECT`, `LAN_GATE_TRUSTED_HOSTS` (public authorities DSH must trust), `LAN_GATE_REWRITE_HOST`, `LAN_GATE_DSH_TOKEN`.
- DSH 0.2 auth: the gateway forwards the browser-facing Host unchanged and mints DSH's signed session cookie with the process launch token (read from `ctx.connection.authenticatedUrl`), so the user opens a plain URL.
- Admin: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/lan-gate/admin — approve/deny/revoke devices, pick phone/desktop/auto.
- Security: first-visit approval (an address is approved, a token identifies a browser), 120 req/min per IP, loopback & LAN bypass.
